head: 06d1059042455b44bc564e490b9f361070ca5fb3
summary:
Fail. The issue outcome is still not delivered.

What is in place: the guarded close checks the exact merge into the default branch, issue identity and contract, and ownership before it would close an issue. It never takes over another owner's claim, and unknown provider results keep the guard and leave the issue open. Existing CI, performance, review, protected-branch, no-bypass and failure-to-todo gates are preserved. No schedule is deployed, and other sessions' worktrees and leases are preserved.

What is still missing:
- recovery_entry.verify_rollout always refuses. Every guarded writer, adoption publisher and recovery wake stops before it closes anything, so a linked issue stays open after an asynchronous merge.
- No hosted asynchronous merge has closed its issue automatically.
- The controlled hosted test of the issues:write permission hypothesis has not been run.
- Actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and safe cancellation are not established.

What this head changes: reconcile now also releases the guard for qualification_not_ready and issue_not_eligible. Both refusals happen before any write, so this is correct.

Defects that remain: other pre-write refusals still keep the guard forever. These include required_gates_not_success (the normal state while CI is pending), review_stale, issue_contract_changed, pr_description_changed and base_changed. Later wakes cannot acquire that guard, so the PR is reported only as guard_unavailable and is never checked again. If CI fails and the issue returns to todo, no worker can reclaim it. Guards for queued or merged requests also have no liveness path.

findings.title: Verified post-merge closure remains unreachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout always raises. Every guarded path, and recovery itself, stops before any issue write, so linked issues stay open after an asynchronous merge.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout-evidence verifier. Deploy recovery through reviewed policy adoption. Then demonstrate an automatic close.

findings.title: Guard retained forever for CI-pending and other pre-write holds
findings.detail: safe_holds now also covers qualification_not_ready and issue_not_eligible. It does not cover other refusals raised by verify before any write: required_gates_not_success (the normal state while CI is pending), review_stale, issue_contract_changed, pr_description_changed and base_changed. Those rows keep the guard forever. Later wakes fail guarded.begin and only report guard_unavailable, so the PR is never re-evaluated and a CI-failed issue cannot be reclaimed by a worker.
findings.required_fix: Classify every deterministic refusal raised before enqueue writes as releasable. Release after block_held plus settle. Add controls for CI-pending and CI-failed PRs across consecutive wakes.

findings.title: Queued-request guards have no liveness or ownership path
findings.detail: cancel_blocked and settle return 'retained' whenever a request exists or the PR merged without a record. block_unadmitted from a later wake can override a queued PR's success status, and nothing restores it.
findings.required_fix: Bind request provenance to the guard. Implement safe takeover or cancellation and recovery for a merge with no record, with controls.

findings.title: No hosted asynchronous merge, automatic-close proof or permission comparison
findings.detail: All controls are synthetic. The Core #77 fixture records a manual close. The controlled hosted test of the issues:write hypothesis is absent.
findings.required_fix: Run hosted positive and negative asynchronous merge controls that close the linked issue, plus the controlled issues:write comparison.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption unproven
findings.detail: actor_rollout is always 'unknown'. The guard protocol requires every active worker and writer to adopt it.
findings.required_fix: Provide verified actor and launcher adoption evidence bound to the exact policy and runtime.
